concepts.definition: The DESIGN_MODULE profile describes Ontology-first engineering design and preferred realisation structure inside implementation and design modules, with explicit authority, effects, low coupling and semantic non-bleed. Its subject Ontology is an engineering model of a designed boundary.

grounding.quote:
this profile what is
the preferred implementation design discipline

concepts.label: Design-module profile

concepts.definition: The Ontology is one semantic truth. Diagrams, matrices, IACS, public interfaces, schemas, architecture, modules, implementation and proof inventories preserve that truth as projections; their presence does not make them independent semantic authorities.

grounding.quote:
The Ontology is one semantic truth (P1, P6; rc.2 #ontology-projection-law).
These preserve it and do not become independent semantic authorities:

concepts.label: Ontology

concepts.definition: An atomic function family is a parameterised semantic operation derived from the Ontology to make entity lifecycles logically complete. Its derivation evidence associates discovered functionality with entity, atomic function or template, higher-order composition, effect class, required authority and disposition.

grounding.quote: | Discovered functionality | Entity | Atomic function or template | Higher-order composition | Effect class | Required authority | Disposition |

concepts.label: Atomic function family

concepts.definition: Higher-order composition is governed by an explicit composition and effect algebra. Typical categories are unit or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and projection.

grounding.quote:
Typical categories include unit
or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold
or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and
projection.

concepts.label: Higher-order composition

concepts.definition: A Prime semantic atom is an irreducible design relation: an atomic function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot honestly be composed from other accepted atoms with the same meaning. Prime is decided at semantic-design altitude.

grounding.quote:
A Prime semantic atom is one irreducible design relation: an atomic
function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation,
topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot be expressed
honestly by composing other accepted atoms while preserving the same
meaning

concepts.label: Prime semantic atom

concepts.definition: Whole-family Prime contraction reviews the entire candidate semantic-atom family and every proposed realisation projection. Recursive contraction reviews individual atoms and then their resulting family; local irreducibility or local Prime-conformance does not establish global Prime.

grounding.quote:
Prime review evaluates the complete candidate semantic-atom family and
every proposed realisation projection, not only functions, carriers or
each atom in isolation.

concepts.label: Whole-family Prime contraction

concepts.definition: Realisation projections include functions, classes, carrier types, top-level schema records and modules. A unit can implement several atoms and an atom can project into several units; physical size, separate naming, typing and independent testability do not establish Prime.

grounding.quote:
One atom may project into several realisation
units, and one realisation unit may implement several atoms, provided the
mapping is explicit and introduces no rival meaning or authority.

concepts.label: Realisation projection

concepts.definition: The Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set, IACS, is the smallest lawful top-level carrier family needed for a boundary's real functionality and authority flow. Example roles are source truth, admission, execution, yielded or recovery, effect plan and public projection carriers.

grounding.quote:
The IACS is the smallest
set of carriers required to carry the real functionality and authority
flow of the boundary.

concepts.label: Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set

concepts.definition: A Subordinate Payload is detail inside a boundary, not top-level by default. The Promotion Test is the explicit test preceding promotion to a top-level type. Boundary Inflation is promotion of subordinate detail into extra peer types without irreducible need.

grounding.quote:
- Subordinate Payload: payload detail that exists inside that boundary but
  is not top-level by default;
- Promotion Test: the explicit test a Subordinate Payload passes before it
  becomes a top-level type; and
- Boundary Inflation: the defect where subordinate payload detail is
  promoted into extra peer types without irreducible need.

concepts.label: Subordinate Payload, Promotion Test and Boundary Inflation

concepts.definition: The three-view design asset contains a structural domain classDiagram, behavioural execution sequenceDiagram and lifecycle stateDiagram-v2. These are fidelity-checked Ontology projections and jointly a sign-off surface for domain identity, authority, behaviour, lifecycle and axiom conformance.
concepts.label: Three-view design asset

concepts.definition: Invariant reconstruction uses two distinct inputs: the selected method basis specifies required relations and reasoning law; accepted design supplies concrete invariant values. Its four decisions about an action against one governing relation are preserves, changes, duplicates and violates, mapped to core values for the specific acting-frame admissibility predicate.

grounding.quote:
the selected method describes which relations
are required and how to reason about them; the accepted design supplies
the concrete invariant values.

concepts.label: Invariant reconstruction and action decisions

concepts.definition: Cross-view axiom assessment has domain verdicts pass, fail and reasoned not_applicable, or directly recorded core values when no domain verdict is reached. Its predicate is that on the exact Ontology and design basis the design meets the axiom OR the axiom does not apply; non-application is distinct from conformance.

grounding.quote:
on the exact
Ontology and design basis, the boundary's design meets the axiom, or the
axiom does not apply to the boundary

concepts.label: Cross-view axiom assessment

concepts.definition: Ontology and design verdicts are separate acceptance results owned by the design authority. Each consumes availability and assessment results. accepted is the disposition accept, mapping to satisfied for the candidate's acceptance at its declared design-gate boundary; production of a pack or passing assessments is not that decision.

grounding.quote:
The Ontology verdict and the design verdict are each an acceptance
result: a decision that consumes the results of assessment, distinct from
them.

concepts.label: Ontology and design acceptance

concepts.definition: The subordinate computational realisation projection exposes abstract data types, identity/key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation/effect boundaries, selected implementations and domain-to-computational mappings. Material components carry explicit semantic and operational role sets; computational similarity identifies commonisation candidates without deciding semantic identity, ownership or authority.

grounding.quote:
the design projects the
domain design into its computational realisation: abstract data types,
identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and
effect boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational
mappings.

concepts.label: Computational realisation projection

concepts.definition: Recommended module roles are carrier (typed immutable inputs, outputs, contracts, transitions, records or envelopes), semantic kernel (main carrier transforms without effects), effect shell (event emission, files, network, subprocesses, persistence or operator delivery), projection (read models/reports from authoritative truth), binding/adapter (external/internal conversion without inventing law), and constructor/materialisation (generated/built artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans). Boundaries support finite-context reasoning, ownership/consumption/emission/proof review and visibility of recurrence.

grounding.quote:
modules should be
classified by role (P0, P6; rc.2 #6-design-module-taxonomy). Recommended
roles are:

concepts.label: Module taxonomy

concepts.definition: Product semantic functions return Product domain outcomes; evaluations consuming those outcomes return their own method core results. These result domains remain distinct even when explicit closed outcome carriers are preferred.

grounding.quote:
The outcome values a
semantic function returns are the Product's domain values, not results of
this method; an evaluation that consumes them returns its own core value

concepts.label: Product outcomes and method results

concepts.definition: Governance surfaces describe state, boundary and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor should work. Lawful governance publications include current state, preserved structure, unmet pressure or unresolved identities, route eligibility, lawful edit/proof frontier, admitted policy identity and prior-turn/run continuity.

grounding.quote:
Governance surfaces describe the state, boundary
and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor
should do the work.

concepts.label: Governance and strategy surfaces

concepts.definition: A recurring realisation pattern across more than one processed boundary is a commonisation candidate. Such candidates are usually not Product truth, authority-neutral, reused across two or more tickets or module boundaries and consumable via local adapters without semantic ownership change. Examples include expectation derivation, nested contract/policy carriers, proof fixtures, effect request/plan shapes and constructors that do not own semantic law.

grounding.quote:
When the same realisation pattern appears across more than one processed
boundary, review treats that pattern as a commonisation candidate rather
than as another purely local clean-up

concepts.label: Recurrence and commonisation candidate

concepts.definition: Post-ticket design review checks the causal closure of the exact declared claim against governing requirements, accepted Ontology, Prime atoms, IACS, views, target modules, implementation and module-owned proof. It is bounded to the claim rather than the whole Product or construction history.

grounding.quote:
The complete selected function is the causal closure of the declared
claim, not the whole Product or the whole history of its construction.

concepts.label: Bounded post-ticket design review

concepts.definition: The functional realisation checklist is a language-agnostic review surface for claims of functional bias, pure transforms, immutable carriers, single-owner truth or low coupling. It covers module, carrier and data-entity design and realisation review, with a compact hard gate for new or materially changed boundaries.

grounding.quote:
When a project claims functional bias, pure transforms, immutable
carriers, single-owner truth or low-coupling realisation, review
explicitly checks

concepts.label: Functional realisation checklist

concepts.definition: Source dispositions are authored provenance and conservation claims about predecessor rc.2 DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD rows and one IDENTITY_METHOD row. Anchors default to the predecessor design member, loci to the receiving file unless named otherwise. A route is provenance only, and a conserved row is claimed to be restated at its receiving locus.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row
is restated in the receiving member's own text; a route is provenance
only.

concepts.label: Source disposition register

concepts.definition: The theoretical Markov-object framing treats a stable self-bounding pattern as a candidate identity-bearing cut whose effective blanket separates identity-bearing from contextual support. It analogises IACS to the smallest lawful identity-bearing cut, payload promotion to independent boundary authority, inflation to mistaking fragments for peers, and strong typing to keeping the cut explicit. This framing is justification, not a prerequisite or scope expansion.

grounding.quote:
It treats a Markov object
as a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern whose
effective blanket separates what is load-bearing for identity from what is
load-bearing for context.

concepts.label: Optional Markov-object framing

concepts.definition: A consumer-bound ABG-role realisation under the graph-execution profile may supply default identity generators, validators and normalisers for its runtime surfaces and default ODD surface kinds used by default F_D helpers.

grounding.quote:
A consumer-bound realisation of the ABG role under the graph-execution
profile may publish default identity generators, validators and
normalisers for its own runtime surfaces and for the default ODD surface
kinds used by default `F_D` helpers

concepts.label: Bound-runtime identity defaults

concepts.definition: EVALUATION is described as a Tier 1 member owning claim justification and acceptance, evidence, independent assessment, review results, realisation conformance and equivalence, frame/method qualification and actual-use evidence of adequate attention. It consumes FOUNDATIONS core results and defines no result values of its own.

grounding.quote:
Tier 1. Owns how claims are justified and accepted: claims, evidence,
independent assessment, review results, acceptance, conformance of
realisations and the equivalence ladder, the qualification of frames and
of the method itself, and actual-use evidence of adequate attention.
Consumes [FOUNDATIONS](FOUNDATIONS.md), whose
[Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) own the core result values this member
uses; it defines no result values of its own.

concepts.label: EVALUATION member

concepts.definition: A load-bearing claim specifies exact subject, claimed property, governing basis, witness-to-claim relation, excluded nearest weaker property and falsifier before selecting a witness. Without this specification the activity is evidence discovery, not proof.

grounding.quote:
A load-bearing claim names its exact subject, the property claimed, the
governing basis, the relation between witness and claim, the nearest weaker
property it excludes, and its falsifier, before a witness is selected.
Without these it is evidence discovery, not proof.

concepts.label: Load-bearing claim

conditions: Higher-order algebra declarations apply where the boundary has higher-order behaviour.

grounding.quote:
Every row is one of: derived through an admitted atomic function; derived
through a declared higher-order composition; deferred with an owner and
re-entry condition; excluded by current product authority; or unresolved
as a named gap

constraints.statement: Derive the smallest parameterised atomic families making lifecycles logically complete. Variation only in entity kind, projection kind, transition kind, policy or subordinate payload should normally be a typed parameter or closed variant, not a peer function. The minimum derivation matrix uses all seven declared columns. Every functionality row is derived through an admitted atomic function, derived through declared composition, deferred with owner and re-entry condition, excluded by current Product authority, or unresolved as a named gap. For higher-order behaviour name the governing composition/effect algebra and applicable identity, closure, associativity, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws explicitly rather than hiding them in controller flow. No private helper, loop, adapter or endpoint may become an undeclared constructor.

conditions: Iterative discovery or retained implementation crosses an affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation.
exceptions: Before design acceptance, a disposable spike may supply evidence when co_evolution_admissible(B) does not hold.

grounding.quote:
Composition, effects and implementation may be discovered iteratively only
when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds. Otherwise only a disposable spike
may supply evidence across the affected unresolved, contradictory or
materially non-equivalent relation before its design is accepted. Every
retained result is reconciled into accepted design before promotion or
design-method closure.

constraints.statement: Iterative discovery of composition, effects and implementation is permitted only under co_evolution_admissible(B). Otherwise the affected relation is design-gated before retained implementation establishes it. Every retained result must be reconciled into accepted design before promotion or design-method closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The full definition of co_evolution_admissible(B) is outside the supplied body sections.

exceptions: An out-of-domain case may justify proposing another candidate atom for design admission.

grounding.quote:
An atom without a declared admitted domain remains a candidate
atom; it cannot supply Prime acceptance or Prime-conformance to a
realisation projection.

constraints.statement: Smallness, typing, separate names or independent testability do not make a file, source function, class, schema record, public operation, diagram, module or owner category Prime. Many-to-many atom/unit mappings must be explicit and introduce no rival meaning or authority. An atomic function is not proven Prime until the complete candidate family is contracted. Every accepted atom declares its admitted domain and governs every admitted instance within it. Later use composes or parameterises it, never locally forks, shadows, specialises or reinterprets it. An in-domain counterexample falsifies the shared atom and requires re-entry at its design boundary, not a feature-local replacement. Without a declared domain it remains a candidate and supplies neither Prime acceptance nor projection Prime-conformance.

conditions: Before promotion; recurrence is contracted during design when visible.

grounding.quote:
A family of individually plausible functions is not Prime when one
parameterised template plus closed variants carries the same meaning and
authority. Recurrence is contracted during design when visible; the
post-implementation recurrence rule (§10) is not a substitute for this
prior pass

constraints.statement: Review includes every proposed identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, function, composition law, effect, closure law and every realisation projection. A function-and-carrier-only pass is insufficient. Review asks whether operations are parameters of one function, commands transitions of one entity, reads projections of one truth, implementations applications of one higher-order function; whether candidates add independent identity, authority, effect, lifecycle, reuse or public pattern-match semantics; whether every atom kind entered contraction; whether every unit maps explicitly to accepted atoms; and whether projections introduce, duplicate or reinterpret meaning or authority. Individually plausible functions fail family Prime when one parameterised template with closed variants carries the same meaning and authority.

conditions: At a material semantic boundary.
exceptions: Work inside an accepted boundary cites the existing Prime basis rather than recreating it.

grounding.quote:
Contraction preserves root authority and every retained semantic relation.
Reducing files, functions, operations or authoring surfaces cannot
compensate for introducing another authority source or truth path

constraints.statement: Contract each candidate atom and then the complete resulting family. Local irreducibility and local projection conformance do not prove global Prime if the family duplicates identity, authority, function, lifecycle, topology, effect or projection meaning. Preserve root authority and every retained semantic relation; surface-count reductions cannot compensate for new authority sources or truth paths. Prime evidence states the complete candidate family; each atom's stable identity, irreducible relation, admitted domain and falsification condition; whole-family contraction; retained meaning and authority before/after; accepted loss; and an explicit total mapping from every proposed realisation projection to accepted atoms.

exceptions: Implementation branches and test expectations need not be enumerated by the Ontology.

grounding.quote:
If a public operation, sequence message, state transition, carrier or
effect cannot be traced through accepted design to the accepted Ontology,
it is ungrounded design and does not enter the active product line.

constraints.statement: Class/domain, sequence and state/lifecycle diagrams; authority/effect matrices; IACS; APIs, registers, SDK/CLI surfaces; schemas, codecs, manifests/catalogues; architecture/module design; implementation through accepted target design; and test/proof inventories through requirements and accepted design preserve one Ontology. Each design projection identifies its source and preserved identity, relationship, lifecycle, authority, function or effect law. Intentional omission/flattening declares accepted loss and a failure condition. Target design may add structural HOW but no rival meaning. Implementation/tests trace through accepted design; branches and expectations trace to requirements plus that design. An untraceable public operation, message, transition, carrier or effect is ungrounded and excluded from the active Product line.

grounding.quote:
A top-level realisation unit is Prime-conformant only when it projects one
or more accepted Prime atoms without introducing, duplicating or
reinterpreting semantic authority. A topological or effect boundary is
first derived and accepted as a Prime atom. Source-code size and
one-to-one correspondence with an atom are immaterial

constraints.statement: Derive Prime atoms from the logically complete candidate Ontology before proposing top-level units; whole-family Prime is evidence for accepting the Ontology basis. Target design, IACS, modules, source functions, schemas and tests project accepted atoms rather than originate Prime meaning. Typed closure alone does not justify a top-level type. Top-level Prime-conformance requires projection of accepted atoms without introducing, duplicating or reinterpreting semantic authority; topological/effect boundaries first require atom derivation and acceptance. Typical lawful reasons are new feature topology/work-graph branch, typed carrier transform, effect boundary, validation/admission boundary or projection boundary. Solely shortening calls, aggregating unrelated behaviour, renaming old interfaces, adding wrappers, hiding mutation/fallback/orchestration, naming authority-free payload variants, exposing internal detail without irreducibility, cosmetic carrier mirroring or multiplying peers for typing discomfort is non-conformant. Prefer composition, existing lawful functions and fewer sharper boundaries/carrier families; the purpose is avoiding fragmentation and helper sprawl, not minimising lines.

grounding.quote:
contraction is not
successful when it increases authority centres, maintained truth surfaces,
acceptance boundaries, dependency cycles, manually reconciled projections
or review burden.

constraints.statement: Apply the referenced ACTIVATION §6 proportionality relation weighing ambiguity removed against reasoning complexity introduced. Review cuts, realisation units, runtime modules and work items are distinct, may map many-to-one or one-to-many and must not be forced one-to-one for administration. Review counts governance cost as well as implementations. Increasing any named authority, truth, acceptance, dependency-cycle, manual-reconciliation or review burden defeats successful contraction. Evidence stays proportional to semantic change and risk; no artifact or review per concern is required.
constraints.uncertainty: The full proportionality relation is not supplied.

conditions: When defining a schema, carrier family or typed public boundary.
exceptions: Ontology, carrier evidence, implementation and tests may develop together when co_evolution_admissible(B) holds.

grounding.quote:
If the accepted Ontology
or IACS has not been declared, the schema is not yet design-method
complete under this profile.

constraints.statement: Derive IACS from accepted Ontology before naming subordinate payloads or implementation modules; it should also precede helper results and internal branch detail. Branch-specific payloads, persistence detail, read-model rows or typing-only field groupings do not automatically justify top-level carriers. Required evidence cites accepted Ontology/function derivation, declares IACS, maps every carrier to its identity/lifecycle/function/authority/effect/projection law, distinguishes authoritative/downstream carriers, defaults all other shapes to Subordinate Payload, keeps them private unless the Promotion Test passes, and reconciles typed implementation before closure. IACS projects rather than replaces Ontology or originates meaning. Missing accepted Ontology or declared IACS prevents schema design-method completeness. Implementation may expose missing meaning but cannot self-ratify it; Ontology/IACS acceptance and reconciliation precede promotion/closure. In design-gated sequencing, accept affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relations before retained implementation establishes them.
constraints.uncertainty: ASSURANCE's binding of conformance tests and unit proof to this carrier inventory is referenced but its full clauses and the member-head binding are absent.

conditions: For every carrier addition, removal, merge or split.
constraints.statement: IACS is not numerically frozen; revision is lawful through accepted Ontology and design re-entry. Accepted design re-derives the entire set and classifies each change; reruns promotion and inflation checks over the full set; updates every checker/conformance subject to the declared composite carrier relation under EVALUATION's congruence and freeze/revision law; and reconciles implementation before promotion or closure. A prohibition lacking a lawful revision path is false. A revision is false if gates inspect only new carriers, assurance retains weaker/obsolete subjects, or implementation is unreconciled before closure.
constraints.uncertainty: EVALUATION §1 is supplied; its referenced §3 freeze/revision provisions are not.

conditions: Promotion of a Subordinate Payload to a top-level class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record.

grounding.quote:
A Subordinate Payload may
be promoted to a top-level type only when at least one of these is true:
it is an authoritative source carrier; it is a public or persisted
contract boundary; it is an explicit variant of a public outcome family
that consumers pattern-match directly; it is reused across several modules
without semantic bleed; or it is versioned, published or admitted
independently.

constraints.statement: A top-level type must justify an architectural boundary. Promotion requires at least one stated ground: authoritative source, public/persisted contract, directly pattern-matched public outcome variant, reuse across several modules without semantic bleed, or independent versioning/publication/admission. These are necessary grounds, not unconditional permission overriding other law. Promotion is unlawful for only internal detail of a larger carrier, a once-used field grouping in one module, an open-dictionary typing shim, a private variant crossing no true interface, or a cosmetic/local mirror. A shape needing no independent authority, reuse or direct pattern-match semantics remains nested/private/local. Proof burden is on promotion; reviewers/designers should assume subordination until an irreducible boundary is shown.

conditions: Schema work; the explicit IACS/payload distinction also applies when a schema or ticket lists a wide type family.

grounding.quote:
If a schema or ticket lists a wide family of types, it
distinguishes the IACS from the Subordinate Payloads; failing to make that
distinction is design drift. Typed closure does not excuse Boundary
Inflation.

constraints.statement: Declare IACS, authoritative types, downstream projections, subordinate shapes and payloads intentionally deferred from promotion. Inflation is design debt when typing difficulty promotes detail into peers, internal records become public without a new authoritative boundary, near-identical top-level types replace one sufficient family, or one migration silently becomes several parallel schema migrations. Typed closure is no excuse; distinguishing IACS from payloads prevents design drift and migration proliferation.

conditions: A realisation is derived from an existing design line, released tenant or reference implementation.

grounding.quote:
The required derivation
evidence is: (1) constitutional WHAT; (2) reference design; (3) target
Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping; (4) target design mapping; (5)
target module boundary assets; (6) implementation.

constraints.statement: Code comparison alone cannot establish design-method completion. Required derivation runs from constitutional WHAT through reference design, target Ontology/reference mapping, target design mapping and module assets to implementation. Minimum assets name reference source surfaces; accepted target Ontology with dispositions of reference entities, functions, lifecycle, authority, effects and projections; replacing/binding target surfaces; explicit preservation, reshaping, deferral or demotion-to-delivery mapping; and target boundary assets including Ontology-derived IACS and three-view design. The question concerns the target boundary's lawful derivation without incidental drift, not merely porting files. An absent chain leaves the target design-method incomplete.

conditions: Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary.
exceptions: Unchanged boundaries cite accepted bases; local realisation with no material semantic-boundary delta does not recreate the gate.

grounding.quote:
Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary carries
one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view Mermaid design asset
before the boundary is promoted or claims design-method closure

constraints.statement: One accepted Ontology and one complete three-view asset precede promotion or design-method closure. Evidence, implementation and tests may co-develop only under co_evolution_admissible(B); otherwise accept affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relations before retained implementation establishes them. All three distinct models and cross-view checks are required; one broad flowchart is insufficient. Views are fidelity-checked projections, not decorative or peer truth surfaces.

exceptions: Ontology evidence may be included or referenced.

grounding.quote:
entity and
relationship inventory; invariant and cardinality law; entity-lifecycle
completeness matrix; authority matrix; atomic-function and
higher-order-function derivation matrix; governing composition and effect
algebra where applicable; whole-family Prime contraction, including every
accepted atom's admitted domain and realisation-projection mapping; and
explicit deferred, excluded and unresolved functionality.

constraints.statement: The design asset cites one accepted Ontology for the active boundary and includes/references entity and relationship inventory, invariant/cardinality law, entity-lifecycle matrix, authority matrix, atomic/higher-order derivation matrix, applicable composition/effect algebra, whole-family contraction with every accepted atom's domain and projection mapping, and deferred/excluded/unresolved functionality. A bounded slice of a wider accepted Ontology cites its parent and preserves parent identity, relationship, lifecycle, authority and function law. Copying rows without that derivation creates another truth surface.

conditions: Given an accepted material-frame basis and declared bounded action, over that action's causally closed affected set.

grounding.quote:
the
selected method basis together with the accepted design is sufficient to
recover every governing relation in the action's causally closed affected
set, and to decide whether the action preserves, changes, duplicates or
violates each of those relations.

constraints.statement: Method basis plus accepted design must recover every governing affected relation and decide preserves/changes/duplicates/violates for each. Neither input substitutes for the other; design must not duplicate method decision law. Durable reasoning state cannot be dialogue, commentary, prior-agent memory or implementation folklore. Sufficiency is action/set-bounded, not about all future changes or reviewer performance. It adds no artifact: existing Ontology evidence, authority matrix, transformation-admission relation, frame declaration, views and module mapping carry it. Missing governing relations or decisions unrecoverable without excluded history falsify the law. Tests, when performed, use named cases with known relations/expected decisions and withhold conversation, commentary, memory and folklore.

conditions: Predicate: the action is admissible in the acting frame on the current governing basis.
exceptions: An evaluation reaching none of the four decisions returns the core value selected by its cause rather than inventing a decision.

grounding.quote:
| preserves | leaves the relation intact and operates inside it | `satisfied` |
| changes | alters the relation itself, and therefore re-enters at that relation before acceptance | `invalid_basis` |
| duplicates | establishes an equivalent path that is explicitly disposed as a constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realisation | `satisfied` |
| violates | contradicts the relation, or establishes an equivalent path that is left undisposed | `falsified` |

constraints.statement: preserves leaves the accepted relation intact and maps to satisfied. changes alters the relation, requires re-entry and change at its own locus before action acceptance, and maps to invalid_basis on the current acting-frame basis. duplicates maps to satisfied only for an equivalent path explicitly disposed as constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realisation. violates maps to falsified for contradiction or an undisposed equivalent path. Acceptance locus, not delta size, separates changes from violates: accepting an otherwise lawful relation change inside the acting frame is a violation. Disposition, not equivalence, separates duplicates from violates. Values travel with both predicate and decision. Insufficient admissible evidence yields indeterminate with what would decide; insufficiency specifically of the selected method/design falsifies reconstruction sufficiency. Lawful change is neither violation nor locally acceptable; violation is not re-entry.

conditions: For the active boundary; boundary-crossing functions and boundary-shaping higher-order relationships where applicable.

grounding.quote:
The standard stereotype vocabulary is `<<prime-conformant>>`,
`<<subordinate>>`, `<<effect-edge>>`, `<<deferred>>`, `<<authoritative>>`
and `<<downstream>>`. The standard visibility vocabulary is `+` public or
exported and `-` module-local or private. The standard relationship
expectations are composition for owned subordinate payloads, association
for downstream consumption, and inheritance only for real variant or
outcome families

constraints.statement: The structural domain view shows identities/cardinalities rather than helper decomposition; ownership, invariants and lawful lifecycle relationships; crossing atomic-family inputs/outputs; boundary-shaping composition; IACS and Prime mappings; subordinate, effect-edge-only, downstream-only and deferred-outside-slice families; authoritative/downstream roles; public/local visibility; and composition, containment, association and actual variants. Use the six standard stereotypes and + public/exported, - module-local/private meanings. Standard relationship expectations are composition for owned subordinate payloads, association for downstream consumption and inheritance only for real variant/outcome families.

conditions: Malformed input/output, retry, recursion, fan-out/fan-in, nested workflow and human escalation paths are shown where applicable.
exceptions: A sequence participant may be an explicitly external actor rather than a domain-model entity.

grounding.quote:
Every
message also binds to an Ontology function and its admitted authority
role; actor identity or call reachability alone does not authorise a
message

constraints.statement: The behavioural view follows admitted input to result or truthful stop and names owner/required authority at every decision, admission, execution, projection and effect boundary. Every participant is in the domain model or explicitly external. Every message binds to a declared carrier transform, graph/computation constructor, interpreter action or effect-handler call, and also to an Ontology function and admitted authority role. Private loops, service methods, plugins, shells or scripts cannot silently replace declared transitions. Actor identity and reachability alone confer no message authority.

conditions: Controller-local memory prohibition applies when the Product declares replay, event, graph or carrier ownership.

grounding.quote:
It shows the complete admitted lifecycle for
the active boundary, including refusal, blocked, continuation, retry,
escalation and terminal states that the boundary can produce. Every
transition binds to an Ontology function and names its owning authority,
admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection or external act.
Controller-local memory is not a lawful source of lifecycle truth when the
product declares replay, event, graph or carrier ownership

constraints.statement: The lifecycle view shows the complete admitted active-boundary lifecycle, including every refusal, blocked, continuation, retry, escalation and terminal state the boundary can produce. Each transition binds to an Ontology function and names its owning authority, admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection or external act. Where replay/event/graph/carrier ownership is declared, controller-local memory cannot supply lifecycle truth.

conditions: Every applicable product, graph, language, runtime, handler and module axiom; graph-algebra visibility applies to graph-native work.
exceptions: Sequence-model prose explicitly permits external actors; the cross-view formulation says every sequence participant exists in the domain model.

grounding.quote: | Axiom | Ontology evidence | Authority | Domain evidence | Sequence evidence | State evidence | Native enforcement | Admission/compiler enforcement | Verdict | Gap owner |

constraints.statement: Use the ten minimum columns and evaluate applicable axioms. The claimed cross-view proof covers Ontology derivation of every element; derived/deferred/excluded/gap functionality disposition; domain existence of sequence participants and lifecycle carriers; declared semantic/effect message boundaries; transitions derivable from admitted truth; explicit function/transition authority paths with no implicit composition widening; public operations as function projections rather than semantic peers; no raw probabilistic output directly accepted/closed; handler/plugin interiors only with runtime ownership of admission, events, continuation and closure; native enforcement of locally decidable relations; and admission/semantic compilation ownership of global references, completeness and realisation gaps. In graph-native work every batch, retry, recursion and nested workflow is visible in the declared graph/compute algebra. A relied-on semantic_not_realized constructor is a blocking gap, never replaced by imperative plugin/shell/service/script/test-harness glue.
constraints.uncertainty: The participant wording has an unresolved scope tension with the sequence-view external-actor exception.

conditions: Values apply to the exact design-meets-axiom OR non-application predicate.

grounding.quote:
| `pass` | the cited Ontology, view and enforcement evidence establishes that the design meets the axiom | `satisfied` |
| `not_applicable` | the axiom's applicability premise is false for the active boundary on basis-bound facts, and the reason names those facts and the authority whose scope declaration excludes the axiom ([ACTIVATION §1 Applicability](ACTIVATION.md#applicability)) | `satisfied` |
| `fail` | the axiom applies, and the evidence names an element, message, transition, authority path or enforcement that violates it; that is the counterexample | `falsified` |

constraints.statement: pass maps to satisfied only with cited Ontology/view/enforcement evidence establishing conformance. not_applicable maps to satisfied only for this disjunction, never for conformance; it requires a false applicability premise on basis-bound facts and a reason naming facts and excluding scope authority. Unresolved applicability cannot support not_applicable. fail maps to falsified when the axiom applies and evidence names a violating element/message/transition/authority path/enforcement counterexample. Record verdict with value. With no domain verdict, record the cause-selected core value and what would decide: indeterminate for undecidable admissible evidence, including unresolved applicability with no conformance; out_of_frame for undeclared required relation/evaluator capability; invalid_basis for unusable Ontology/design basis. An applicable unevaluated axiom has no result. None is pass; excluded, undecided and unevaluated are not converted to conformance or failure.

conditions: New or semantically changed boundaries, and affected promotion, publication or design-method closure.
exceptions: An unchanged realization_refactor reuses the verdict after citing the accepted bases, identifying touched projections and proving no entity, relationship, lifecycle, authority, function, effect or public-semantic delta.

grounding.quote:
An axiom whose result
is not `satisfied`, whether `fail` or a core value recorded directly, an
applicable axiom with no result, or an axiom with no result whose
applicability is not established false, keeps the verdict non-accepted
as a failed axiom does

constraints.statement: Both Ontology and design verdicts must be accepted before affected implementation, public contract or semantic carrier promotion or closure. Failed applicable axioms, missing functionality dispositions, unresolved authority paths and blocking realisation gaps prevent acceptance. So do every non-satisfied axiom result, applicable axiom without a result, and no-result axiom whose applicability is not established false. Acceptance is the design authority's disposition consuming availability, decision-completeness assessment, axiom results and cross-view proofs; neither a fully passing matrix nor producing the pack supplies acceptance. Non-accepted means another referenced disposition or no disposition yet; the latter is no acceptance result. Missing Ontology, any view, cross-view evaluation or either accepted verdict means incompleteness and bars promotion/publication/closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The other three ACTIVATION dispositions and full decision-completeness acceptance criterion are not supplied.

conditions: Co-evolution or retrospective review of existing implementation.
exceptions: Without co_evolution_admissible(B), only a disposable spike may cross an affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation before acceptance.

grounding.quote:
newly discovered material ambiguity,
contradiction or a materially non-equivalent network makes
`decision_complete(B)` false and activates the design gate for that
decision. Promotion and design-method closure remain blocked until the
required Ontology, three-view asset and axiom evaluation are accepted.

constraints.statement: Under co_evolution_admissible(B), implementation may precede/co-develop with evidence and be retained after reconciliation, but before gate acceptance it is provisional evidence with no semantic authorship, publication authority, promotion or closure standing. Existing code may inform retrospective design. Material ambiguity, contradiction or a materially non-equivalent network makes decision_complete(B) false and activates the affected decision's gate; acceptance of Ontology, views and axiom evaluation is required before promotion/closure. Evaluate code against prior authority, never rewrite design to rationalise unlawful code. Keep assets boundary-bounded; mixing unrelated bootstrap, test-harness, projection or delivery shapes merely to appear complete is a defect.

conditions: Every material component; computational projection at a material semantic boundary; complete-path accounting for material producer-to-consumer paths.
exceptions: Behaviour within an already abstract declared role is ordinary variation and does not itself require re-entry.

grounding.quote:
A component may
lawfully hold several roles. Three cases are distinguished: behaviour
already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation; a new
operational responsibility and a new semantic or authoritative role are
each design changes, and only those two require re-entry.

constraints.statement: Declare explicit semantic/operational role sets; several roles are lawful, technology capability confers no authority, and authority-bearing roles preserve their applicable authority relations through composition/use. A new operational responsibility or semantic/authoritative role requires design re-entry. Out-of-role use cannot silently establish identity, admission, lifecycle, ordering, closure or projection truth. Cross-view evaluation extends to show one system across domain and computational projections. Material producer-to-consumer paths identify fact establishment, consumers, basis/invalidators, effects, retained alternatives and accumulated work, including material method/assurance operations. Component-local success cannot prove complete-path claims; different names do not prove different responsibilities.
constraints.uncertainty: IDENTITY §6, ACTIVATION §4/§7 and ASSURANCE §13 are referenced supporting laws whose complete bodies are absent.

conditions: Material algorithmic work; acceptance limits are bound before qualification.
exceptions: No extra accounting system or fixed algorithmic complexity is required.

grounding.quote:
Bind
any acceptance limits and their owning authority before qualification;
limits and workloads are Product-owned, not universal method constants.
Challenge the assumptions on representative supported paths and material
growth. Observe work directly where elapsed time cannot locate it, without
repeating the operation merely to count it.

constraints.statement: Declare supported input dimensions, workload/growth and operational assumptions needed for the selected outcome. Startup, framework processing, external computation, transport and assurance cost separation is assigned to ACTIVATION §6. Bind Product-owned limits/workloads and owning authority before qualification; challenge assumptions on representative supported paths and material growth. Observe work directly when elapsed time cannot locate it, without rerunning merely to count. Carry evidence on existing design/proof surfaces.

conditions: Computational similarity or each material algorithmic obligation in M(B).
exceptions: Isolation, substrate, performance, security and dependency ownership are lawful grounds for independent implementations.

grounding.quote:
The invariant is not that equivalent code is never
rebuilt; it is that a local realisation does not present an existing
accepted semantic or authoritative relation as newly owned local truth

constraints.statement: Similarity leads to a candidate, then semantic/operational equivalence evaluation, then reuse, a parameterised common relation or justified separation; it never decides identity/ownership/authority. Material non-equivalence in identity/key law, ownership, ordering, mutation, consistency/concurrency, retention, failure, access policy, lifecycle or truth authority requires separation. Other differences justify separation only when adaptation/parameterisation would weaken ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational constraints; difference alone does not discharge Prime/recurrence review. Every material M(B) algorithmic obligation records semantic disposition (existing relation, extension, new candidate) and realisation disposition (consume, local implementation, optimise, adapt, or deliberate duplication under stated non-semantic constraints). The law is false for equivalent machinery without semantic disposition, generic blocks becoming semantic authority, commonising despite different governing laws, or local implementations claiming accepted relations as newly owned truth.
constraints.uncertainty: M(B)'s full membership is not supplied.

grounding.quote:
This is a theoretical justification, not an extra prerequisite. The rules
of this profile remain engineering law even where the Markov-object
construct is irrelevant, unavailable or still only candidate-class
(FOUNDATIONS §5). The framing sharpens the ask; it does not expand the
scope of the profile

constraints.statement: Using this operational profile requires neither a world-model domain nor acceptance of an empirical ontology programme, Constraint-Emergence Ontology, world-model theory or metaphysical/empirical claim. Engineering rules retain their stated scope even if the Markov-object construct is irrelevant, unavailable or candidate-class.

conditions: When this profile governs a realisation boundary.

grounding.quote:
The design-to-module evidence route, the module-derived unit-test rule and
the module lifecycle confirmation rule are assurance law

constraints.statement: Modules should be classified by the recommended roles to bound traversal reasoning, not for naming ceremony. Review should be able to identify ownership, consumption, emission and sufficient proof without rereading the system. Design-to-module evidence, module-derived unit tests and lifecycle confirmation remain ASSURANCE §14/§15/§16 law, applied through the member-head binding, not newly owned rules of this taxonomy.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced assurance clauses and member-head binding are outside the supplied source.

conditions: Projects using this profile.

grounding.quote:
Projects using this profile prefer one algebraic primitive plus
projections over several local decision systems, and prefer total
functions, closed enums, explicit state and deterministic folds (P2, P5,
P6; provenance rc.2 authority_compressions/stdo_compressed.md and
design_module_method.compressed.md, a claim no rc.2 body states).

constraints.statement: Prefer one algebraic primitive plus projections to several local decision systems; prefer total functions, closed enums, explicit state and deterministic folds. This is a preference, with source provenance explicitly assigned to predecessor compressions rather than an rc.2 body statement.

exceptions: Typed immutable source truth is recommended unless mutation is materially necessary.

grounding.quote:
Mutable
carrier state requires explicit justification when it is
performance-critical, required by the host runtime or framework, or
modelling a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth.
Convenience is not sufficient justification.

constraints.statement: Source truth should use typed immutable values unless mutation is materially necessary. Preferred shape: constructor/parser produces a typed carrier; transforms consume one and return another or a closed result; projections read without mutation. Mutable carrier state requires explicit justification for performance-critical, host/runtime-required or genuinely stateful-boundary use rather than semantic truth. Convenience is insufficient.

conditions: To the extent allowed by the language and problem; typed explicit failure when practical.

grounding.quote:
Projects using this profile should prefer
`Result`-like or closed outcome carriers, explicit validation stages, and
explicit "unsupported" or "rejected" outcomes. They should avoid partial
functions that assume hidden preconditions, semantic `.get(...)` fallback
chains, and controller code that reconstructs missing truth from defaults

constraints.statement: Semantic functions should be total or as close as language/problem allow, including encounters outside admitted domains. Prefer boundary rejection of invalid input, kernels consuming admitted carriers only, practical typed explicit failure, Result-like/closed outcomes, explicit validation and unsupported/rejected outcomes. Avoid hidden-precondition partial functions, semantic .get fallback chains and default-based reconstruction of missing truth. Product outcome values remain distinct from method evaluation results.

grounding.quote:
If a function both decides the
semantic meaning and directly performs the write, the design should be
treated as suspect.

constraints.statement: Effects should be explicit and isolated; examples are file writes, network calls, subprocesses, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and database mutation. Kernels should not perform them while deciding law. Prefer admitting/parsing authoritative input, transforming to a typed plan/outcome, applying effects at the edge from that value, then publishing events/projections downstream. A function deciding meaning and directly writing should be treated as suspect.

grounding.quote:
A
module is acting as an unlawful semantic centre when reviewers have to
read it to discover what counts as closure, what identity means, what
failure means, what work is next, or what the current truth is. Those
meanings should already exist in carriers, contracts or explicit design
modules.

constraints.statement: Controllers, managers, service methods, runtime loops and public wrappers should not be hidden semantic centres. This includes procedural meaning in orchestration, truth rebuilt from fragments, current law rehydrated from legacy/fallbacks, and typed meaning flattened into ad hoc dictionaries/.get chains. Needing to inspect such a module to discover closure, identity, failure, next work or current truth identifies an unlawful centre; these meanings should already be explicit in carriers, contracts or design modules.

grounding.quote:
The preferred dependency direction is
`carriers -> semantic kernels -> effect shells -> projections`, not
`controllers -> service helpers -> mutable runtime state -> projections`.

constraints.statement: Coupling should be reduced through dependency shape, not just file count. Preserve the source's preferred carriers -> semantic kernels -> effect shells -> projections direction and rejected controller/helper/mutable-state direction. Excess coupling is indicated by many modules reading/mutating one object, projections inferring truth from implementation state, consumers silently rebuilding source truth from raw artifacts, or tests passing only because several modules duplicate meaning. Reduction means fewer places able to invent meaning.
constraints.uncertainty: The arrows' exact import-direction convention is not defined; the functional checklist separately says semantic algebra depends on carrier contracts.

conditions: A boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another actor, executor, builder or substrate.
exceptions: Imperative strategy is allowed only when strategy ownership is explicitly part of the boundary's ratified responsibility.
Budgets, scores, counters or heuristics may assess another actor's judgment only when that assessment boundary is explicitly owned.

grounding.quote:
When a boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another
actor, executor, builder or substrate, it publishes governance truth, not
imperative strategy law, unless strategy ownership is explicitly part of
the boundary's ratified responsibility

constraints.statement: Publish governance truth within the ratified boundary. Unlawful drift includes downstream repair/action commands, framework preferences disguised as observability, unowned scoring that recreates the actor's judgment, and prompts/reports/read models becoming hidden strategy doctrine. A governance/observability system must not become a replacement decision engine through contexts, projections, prompts or route helpers.

conditions: A boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor or bounded implementation.
exceptions: Cross-boundary implementation may enter separately if admitted by the owning authority at the smallest lawful re-entry point.

grounding.quote:
Opportunistic
optimisation is lawful only when it is boundary-local to the active design
or module surface; behaviour-preserving at the declared semantic boundary;
authority-neutral, with no change to ownership of truth;
visibility-neutral, with no silent promotion of subordinate payloads; and
effect-neutral, with no hidden expansion of runtime, persistence or
bootstrap doctrine.

constraints.statement: The area should be left better, subordinate to constitutional truth, module ownership and functional equivalence. Lawful cleanup must be local, behaviour-preserving, authority-neutral, visibility-neutral and effect-neutral. Examples are removing parser re-entry on local truth, consolidating local routing, replacing local scans/algorithms without semantic change and simplifying proofs/tests without changing module claims. Cross-module lookup/index/cache/persistence repricing; public carrier, visibility or truth-owner changes; wider effects/runtime observability; and performance changes to Product expectations require design re-entry. Cross-boundary discoveries are repricing inputs, not silently absorbed scope. DESIGN_MODULE owns scope separation; TICKETS owns recording/closure mechanics. Cleanup cannot cover unauthorised redesign.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced re-entry and ticket mechanics are not supplied.

conditions: Repeated pattern across more than one processed boundary; special threshold at a third local rebuild.
exceptions: A third rebuild may be conformant if it consumes an existing reusable surface, extends it before local implementation lands, or has an explicit do-not-commonise decision explaining boundary specificity.

grounding.quote:
a third local rebuild
is not design-method conformant unless the active boundary consumes an
existing reusable library or commonisation surface, extends that surface
before the local implementation lands, or review records an explicit
do-not-commonise decision and why the pattern is still boundary-specific

constraints.statement: Treat recurrence as a commonisation candidate, not merely another cleanup. TICKETS §6 owns rule-of-two, third-rebuild threshold/commonisation order and migration-ticket library_usage, governing_library and library_rationale fields; this clause supplies design-review conformance, not another ticket lifecycle. Tenant-local authority-neutral reusable patterns should be extracted under that order. Changes to ownership, public carriers, module boundaries or common law are separate design decisions. Commonisation closes only when the selected path consumes the accepted relation and superseded production responsibility is retired or satisfies the referenced retention relation. Compare removed work and maintained responsibilities across the path; shared names, fewer lines and unused helpers do not establish contraction.
constraints.uncertainty: The full TICKETS commonisation order and SPEC_METHOD retention relation are absent.

conditions: A ticket applies the profile and claims its boundary processed or design-method closed.
exceptions: The check may be part of normal verification and requires no separate artifact, review round or reviewer.

grounding.quote:
Exact hashes establish subject
identity; headings and artifact presence establish location; green tests
establish only the properties they actually assert. None supplies a
missing semantic relation or substitutes a weaker property for the
governed claim

constraints.statement: Closure should not rest on implementation status alone; check the processed boundary against accepted design and the exact claim before closure. Determine current design/module lawfulness; inclusion of every causally applicable live requirement, accepted design relation and retained predecessor claim; competing/ambiguous acceptance-path authority; durable architectural decisions foreclosing admitted Product outcomes; and falsifying issues/hard stops. Reconstruct the complete selected function from requirements through Ontology, Prime, IACS, views, modules, implementation and owned proof rather than only prior findings. Hashes prove subject identity, headings/presence location, tests only asserted properties; none substitutes for missing semantics. TICKETS retains status, closure, reopening, dependencies and follow-up mechanics.

conditions: Reuse of current accepted Ontology, design verdict and sufficient reconstruction evidence for an unchanged boundary.

grounding.quote:
A new role, conversation or review occurrence is not one of
them, so it does not itself require re-authoring that evidence or
recreating the three views. Missing, stale or ambiguous coverage is not a
no-delta proof.

constraints.statement: Confirm exact scope, traces, applicability and absence of ACTIVATION §7's three invalidators; this profile adds no fourth. A governing-source reprice changes the basis only for affected relations/projections pending impact review. An applicable later candidate materially altering the lawful frontier changes selection input; evidence/material dimensions defeating dominance change that relation's input. New roles, conversations or review occurrences alone do not invalidate. Missing/stale/ambiguous coverage is not no-delta proof. Material changed relations or new counterexamples require affected reconstruction and the applicable gate while conserving supported unaffected relations. Reuse never weakens full coverage for new/materially changed boundaries.
constraints.uncertainty: Only changed-basis and material-input-change instances are named here; the complete three-invalidator definition is external.

conditions: Findings from the bounded closure check.
exceptions: Optional cleanup, recurrence, generality and cross-boundary discoveries outside the exact claim remain repricing observations rather than automatic new work.

grounding.quote:
an issue that falsifies the current claim or an
applicable hard stop blocks the design-method closure claim

constraints.statement: Falsifying current-claim issues or applicable hard stops block design-method closure: falsified cannot become satisfied and hard stops are not waived. Current-promotion blocking is separately governed by EVALUATION §5; this profile names falsifying issues, competing authority, unlawful/omissive claims and durable architectural foreclosure as its triggers. Ticket/review wording cannot remove active authority. Absorb cleanup/commonisation only when necessary for current truth, singular authority, accepted design or preventing that foreclosure. Other discoveries neither automatically widen the subject nor block its bounded claim nor require follow-up tickets. Owner-admitted repricing enters at the smallest lawful point. Processed tickets should not claim closure until the bounded check is complete.
constraints.uncertainty: EVALUATION §5's full four-condition rule is not supplied.

grounding.quote:
The required shape: each interface family has
one authoritative source truth; downstream interfaces consume that truth;
crossing an interface boundary does not create a new semantic centre. Low
coupling requires semantic non-bleed, not only small functions.

constraints.statement: Interfaces should not bleed authority across families. Bleed includes reconstructing another interface's source truth, projections deciding closure, reports/prompts deciding admission, wrappers deciding kernel semantics and adapters inventing meaning. Required shape is one authoritative source per family, downstream consumption of that truth and no new semantic centre created by crossing boundaries. Small functions alone do not establish low coupling.

conditions: Projects using the profile.
exceptions: Intentionally retained compatibility is an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof.

grounding.quote:
If compatibility is intentionally retained, it is treated as
an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof; otherwise
the proxy path is removed.

constraints.statement: Do not substitute proxy/partial interfaces for migration or design completion. A new-looking interface forwarding to old authority, reconstructing missing truth from it, preserving its executability under a new name, or keeping proofs green while old law governs is bridge debt. Without explicitly bounded compatibility authority and proof, remove the proxy path.

conditions: Prompts under the profile; provenance/proof requirement applies to clauses intended to enforce design law.

grounding.quote:
A worker may be told where to inspect and what
contract to satisfy. A prompt clause that exists to enforce design law
needs provenance and a proof that the clause still causes or prevents the
intended behaviour

constraints.statement: Prompts follow ACTIVATION §2 context construction. They may identify inspection locations and contracts. Clauses enforcing design law need provenance and proof of continuing causal/preventive effect on intended behaviour. The source attributes this claim to predecessor compression and expressly says no rc.2 body states it.
constraints.uncertainty: The context-construction law and predecessor compression are not supplied.

conditions: Reviewing code under this profile; Python, reference, governance, cleanup, recurrence, ticket and graph questions apply under their stated conditions.

grounding.quote:
If these questions cannot be answered cleanly, the realisation is too
coupled or too imperative

constraints.statement: Ask the listed review questions, preserving their interrogative role: typed semantic ownership versus orchestration; transforms over admitted truth; isolated effects; no projection closure invention or reconstructed rival carriers; justified bounded local mutation; direct source pattern matching; no silent compatibility authority; fail-closed carrier removal; Prime-projected functions; no interface bleed; Python Any/open dictionaries/untyped definitions; declared IACS and justified payload promotion; no inflation/parallel migrations; no increased truth surfaces and reduction of duplicates; no trusted foreign/open payload beyond ingress; proof before enforcement; governance versus strategy; reference-to-target derivation; faithful domain/IACS/Prime/visibility/ownership/deferred mappings; module-derived tests; bounded cleanup and owner-admitted cross-boundary work; explicit recurrence and third-rebuild dispositions; exact closure checks without optional discovery; graph-governed traversal rather than substitution; deterministic operative-edge repricing; F_D/transforms/effect shells subordinate to GTL/ABG; lifecycle confirmation or named Gap:/Unanswered: phases; proper release/deployment/use/telemetry/retirement authority; reasoned lifecycle non-application; three distinct views; participant/message bindings; transitions from admitted truth; complete axiom matrix; blocking semantic_not_realized gaps; justified sequencing and acceptance timing; accepted Ontology before promotion; entity/identity/relation/invariant/lifecycle completeness without default mutable CRUD; applicable proposer/evaluator/verifier/admitter/executor/projector/retirement authority distinct from actor/capability; all functionality disposed; whole-family Prime/domains/mappings; applicable composition identity/closure/cardinality/effect/authority conservation; all downstream surfaces traceable with declared loss; and no hidden meaning exposed by removing Ontology. Inability to answer cleanly is characterised as excessive coupling or imperative design.

conditions: Review of a material generic capability, common mechanic, reused foundation or newly exposed generic subproblem.

grounding.quote:
56. Did any newly exposed material generic subproblem recursively re-enter
    the foundation-selection relation before its implementation was
    retained?

constraints.statement: Questions 49–56 ask whether capability was stated without Product/domain/module/vendor/file/incumbent labels and factored into declared semantic/authority relations versus mechanics; bounded discovery recorded every searched source/category, cutoff/version basis, applicability, exclusions, predecessor/incumbent status and residual unknown with later material-candidate invalidation; credible compositions were compared over relevant lifecycle dimensions without incumbent/source-order/local-code/dependency-count preference; hard authority, contract, safety, security, licensing and constructability failures were eliminative while unknowns stayed explicit; reused roles preserved owner, kind, subject, scope, basis, lifecycle and refusal invariants without authority widening; selection was undominated under evidence with existing trade-off-owner priorities/risk tolerances rather than undefined total ordering; rejected material candidates had decisive evidence/falsifiers and unresolved frontier remained a gap; and new material generic subproblems re-entered selection before retained implementation.
constraints.uncertainty: The full UP-023 foundation-selection body is absent; these are supplied review criteria, not a reconstructed full algorithm.

conditions: Claims of functional bias, pure transforms, immutable carriers, single-owner truth or low-coupling realisation.
exceptions: Reference equivalence/derivation applies when a reference exists; identity ownership when identity is introduced; cleanup, recurrence, closure, cross-boundary and graph checks apply under their respective triggers.
constraints.statement: Explicitly check constitutional WHAT/lawful HOW; one accepted Ontology covering entities through projections; every create/read/update/retire question assigned lawful function, reasoned not_applicable or owned gap; distinct actor/capability and proposal/evaluation/verification/admission/execution/projection/retirement roles; every functionality item disposed without direct verb-to-operation promotion; parameterised whole-family contraction before peer promotion with all atoms/domains/projections; fidelity of IACS/views/contracts/adapters/code/tests; reference semantic equivalence and pre-implementation target mapping; proportional generic foundation selection with discovery/frontier/roles/decisive evidence; common module assets for implementation/tests; one truth owner and reduced duplicate/reconstructed authority; admitted-only pure semantic inputs; no hidden time, randomness, UUIDs, environment, process, filesystem, network or registries; ingress/effect-owned identity; immutable newly returned carriers and no shared mutable semantic state; no reparsing/validation/loading of locally assembled truth; ingress rejection of invalid/incomplete truth; explicit ratified carrier-owned defaults; one clear function owner/responsibility; algebra depending on carrier contracts, admission on validation, effects at edges; no semantic/effect mixing or typed-truth erasure; package/bootstrap/controller/adapter/runtime layers below semantics; governance facts/eligibility/provenance without strategy; complete current views/matrix/accepted verdict without gap bypass; module/IACS-derived tests; bounded cleanup; explicit reuse/extension or boundary-specific/non-candidate rationale; owner-admitted cross-boundary entry; exact-claim closure checks; negative proof that imperative/open-payload/effect-erasure bypass fails closed; graph traversal subordination and repricing for next-work/closure/target-motion/function-identity decisions; lifecycle phases answered, reasoned inapplicable or named gaps; and externally authorised release/deployment/use/telemetry/retirement claims.
constraints.uncertainty: These checklist criteria are retained under their claim trigger; their stricter wording is not silently substituted for the general recommendations elsewhere.

conditions: Compact hard gate for a new or materially changed boundary.
exceptions: For an unchanged boundary, accepted basis plus evidence of no material semantic-boundary delta replaces recreation of Ontology, IACS, views, evaluation or unit-test lane.

grounding.quote:
For an unchanged boundary, the hard gate is the accepted basis plus
evidence of no material semantic-boundary delta; it does not require a new
Ontology, IACS, three-view asset, cross-view evaluation or unit-test lane

constraints.statement: The 14 hard-gate checks are accepted Ontology before promotion/closure and design-gated retained implementation; complete lifecycle/authority/function evidence; whole-family Prime/domains/mappings/composition/effects; proportional generic foundation selection with discovery/frontier/exact role and authority conservation; pure semantic functions; immutable carriers without shared semantic mutation; one owner per truth surface; low admission/algebra/effect coupling; no hidden runtime authority; accepted domain/sequence/state projections; complete axiom evaluation without bypassed gaps; specification and applicable reference equivalence; lifecycle confirmation or named canonical-lifecycle gaps; and negative imperative/open-bypass proof. The checklist is language-agnostic across module, carrier, entity design and realisation review.

conditions: Adoption by Product authority for a named boundary; completion obligations apply to new or materially changed adopted boundaries at the granularity of change.
exceptions: Partial adoption may narrow named scope, but not skip reconstruction/audit/refactor evidence while claiming completion.

grounding.quote:
inclusion in the selected method cut makes the profile available, and only
Product authority adopts it. This profile adds no adopter.

constraints.statement: Availability through a selected method cut is distinct from adoption, which this body assigns only to Product authority. Once adopted, apply consistently across Ontology/architecture derivation, design modules, execution kernels, prompts/reporting, constructors/materialisers and projections/queries. Carrier/schema/governance migrations should explicitly name closure evaluators in the ADR/ticket. New/materially changed adopted boundaries cite accepted Ontology with lifecycle, authority, derivation, whole-family Prime, domains, mappings and traceability before completion. Schema/carrier changes derive and reconcile IACS; reference-derived changes publish reference-to-target and three-view assets; active implementation changes publish a module-derived unit-test lane before closure. Partial adoption should explicitly name boundary and rule family.
constraints.uncertainty: The source disposition register marks the adoption replacement as proposed and pending owner acceptance; this record describes the body rule without treating that proposal as accepted.

conditions: UX refinement only for work realising a UX/UI surface; graph-profile unit selection only for graph-governed Products.

grounding.quote:
The module lifecycle confirmation rule (ASSURANCE §16) detects whether the
realisation has enough lifecycle signal to be safely built and reviewed.
It does not decide release eligibility, exact-cut acceptance, selector
promotion, install policy or operational rollout

constraints.statement: SPEC_METHOD owns constitutional process, authority flow, repricing and migration; RELEASE owns release/Product/install/qualification/version-line promotion and exact-cut/selector decisions; ODD owns graph-native constructive carrier law; DESIGN_MODULE owns preferred internal design structure; UX adds rendering/state/effect rules only on UX surfaces. For graph-governed work ODD selects outcome traversal, graph function, GTL module or ABG runtime boundary; this profile structures deterministic realisation/evaluation/adaptation/projection inside it. UX adds render/reducer purity, effect membranes and AssetSurface binding when applicable. ASSURANCE lifecycle confirmation concerns build/review signal, not release eligibility, exact-cut acceptance, selector promotion, install or rollout, which remain RELEASE/project-owned.
constraints.uncertainty: The other members' complete laws are outside this excerpt.

conditions: Consumer-bound ABG-role realisation under the graph-execution profile.

grounding.quote:
the permission is scoped to that role
and does not extend to other runtime realisations

constraints.statement: The may-publish permission is limited to the bound ABG role's own runtime surfaces and default ODD kinds used by default F_D helpers, not other runtime realisations.
